input.rationale: Promoted the source-visible consequence of an empty reconstruction on the vote path as durable behaviour knowledge, citing the guards themselves: both requestVote and requestPreVote guard their membership and voter rejections behind len(configurations.latest.Servers) > 0, so a node whose reconstruction is empty performs no membership or voter check when it decides whether to grant support.

knowledge.statement: With an empty reconstructed configuration both vote handlers skip their membership and voter rejections: requestVote rejects a candidate absent from the configuration only when len(r.configurations.latest.Servers) > 0 and rejects a candidate without a vote under the same guard, and requestPreVote repeats both guards, so a node holding no servers performs neither check and can grant support to a peer that is neither a member nor a voter of the committed configuration.
knowledge.conditions: The node's configurations.latest is empty while the committed configuration recorded in its own log names members; the request passes the term, leader and log up-to-dateness checks that follow the guards; NewRaft reconstruction with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled can produce such an empty configuration at startup.

knowledge.statement: NewRaft re-derives Raft's own configuration from configuration-carrying log entries only for indices above max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied); the other writers of r.configurations are snapshot restore, snapshot install and the leader's own appendConfigurationEntry path, and nothing else repairs it.
knowledge.conditions: Startup reconstruction in NewRaft over a log store; lastApplied may already be advanced by restoreFromCommittedLogs or by a restored snapshot; configuration entries are identified by LogConfiguration or the deprecated peer entry types.

knowledge.statement: restoreFromCommittedLogs reads the commit index from a CommitTrackingLogStore, clamps it to the last log index, sets the commit index and calls processLogs, which applies the committed prefix to the FSM and sets lastApplied to that commit index; this happens after snapshot restore and before NewRaft's configuration scan.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and the log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore; the tracked commit index is at least the index of a configuration entry stored in the log.

knowledge.statement: The configuration a node holds decides its own participation and support arithmetic: runFollower declines to campaign when latestIndex is zero or the local ID has no vote in the latest configuration, a candidate needs quorumSize() votes of the latest configuration, and the leader's commitment is constructed from the latest configuration, so a stale or empty reconstruction directly changes which support is required and counted.
knowledge.conditions: The configuration is the one reconstructed at startup or later written by a snapshot install or a configuration change; quorumSize and the commitment are computed from configurations.latest.

knowledge.statement: appendEntries processes configuration entries only for the entries it newly appends; entries already present at the same index and term are skipped, so ordinary replication from a healthy leader does not re-derive the configuration of a follower whose log already matches.
knowledge.conditions: Follower handling a normal AppendEntries whose entries are duplicates of its own log; entries that are in the leader's compacted prefix instead arrive as an InstallSnapshot, which rewrites both configurations from the snapshot metadata.

knowledge.statement: A restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled over a commit-tracking log store reconstructs a configuration that is not the one recorded in the node's own log whenever the tracked commit index covers that node's last configuration entry, in both directions and across three ladders: the no-snapshot case reported latest_config_index 0 with no servers against a single-voter entry at log index 1; the snapshot-then-remove case reported the snapshot's two voters, one of them the peer removed at log index 103, against the single-voter entry there; the snapshot-then-promote case reported one voter, the promoted peer still a nonvoter, against the two-voter entry at log index 104; and the three-voter ladder reported one voter against the three-voter entry at log index 106. The public GetConfiguration view reported the same value, and the flag-disabled controls and the within-flag case whose configuration entry sits above the replayed prefix all reconstructed the entry's own index and voter count.
knowledge.conditions: NewRaft restart over the same log, stable and snapshot stores; RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and the log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore; the node's last configuration entry is either inside the applied prefix replayed from the tracked commit index (divergence, in either direction) or above it (correct reconstruction); no membership change is issued after the restart.

history.conditions: NewRaft restart over the same log, stable and snapshot stores with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a commit-tracking log store; no other instance left running and no later membership change. knowledge.statement: In the retained promoted-voter execution, the reconstructed smaller configuration changed what support counted: the restarted instance became Leader while sending no election request at all (election_requests 0, became_leader true, state Leader) although the configuration entry in its own log has two voters, and a subsequent Apply completed (apply_ok true) while the other member of that committed configuration was stopped, so both the leadership decision and the committed decision rested on support from one of the two committed voters; the flag-disabled control over the same availability reported the two-voter configuration, sent 39 election requests, did not become leader, and its Apply failed with "node is not the leader".
knowledge.conditions: Two-member cluster whose committed configuration is a two-voter configuration recorded at log index 104 while the node's snapshot metadata still carries a single-voter configuration; every instance is stopped before the restart, the restarted instance is the only running member, and the commit attempt uses a 1000 ms Apply timeout.

knowledge.statement: In the retained three-voter execution, a commit acknowledged to the client rested on a single copy of the committed configuration: the restarted instance's Apply completed (acknowledged true, payload index 113) while only it held that payload (payload_on_victims 0, durable_copies 1, durable_on_majority false), the two other voters reconstructed their own three-voter configuration and elected new leadership without it, and after the holder rejoined the payload was still present only there (payload_on_holder_after_rejoin true at index 113) with the new leadership formed in the same term as the stale leader (both 3).
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster whose committed configuration entry sits at log index 106 while the restarted instance's snapshot metadata carries a single-voter configuration; every instance is stopped before the restart, the restarted instance is the only running member when it acknowledges the commit, the other two voters are then rebuilt with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled, and the payload is searched for in every store across its first-to-last index.

knowledge.statement: In the retained live-cluster execution a restarted follower no longer held any configuration and ordinary replication did not repair it: after 400 ms of a leader that stayed in Leader state, the follower's reconstructed configuration was empty (latest_config_index 0, no servers) while its own log's configuration entry at index 103 has two voters and its log already matched the leader's (last log index 113, last applied 110, snapshot_count 0). When that leader afterwards appended a new configuration entry at index 114, the follower's configuration became that entry (latest_config_index 114, three voters), so the repair came from the later configuration change rather than from replication; the flag-disabled control over the same shape held latest_config_index 103 with two voters at observation time and was repaired by the same entry.
knowledge.conditions: Three-member cluster whose leader committed a RemoveServer before the restart and kept leading; only the remaining follower was restarted, over its own stores and with no snapshot of its own, reconnected to the live leader in both directions; the observation and repair windows are 400 ms each.

func (r *Raft) setupLeaderState() {
	r.leaderState.commitCh = make(chan struct{}, 1)
	r.leaderState.commitment = newCommitment(r.leaderState.commitCh,
		r.configurations.latest,
		r.getLastIndex()+1 /* first index that may be committed in this term */)
	r.leaderState.inflight = list.New()
	r.leaderState.replState = make(map[ServerID]*followerReplication)
	r.leaderState.notify = make(map[*verifyFuture]struct{})
	r.leaderState.stepDown = make(chan struct{}, 1)
}

	MonotonicLogs      bool

	PropagateError     bool // If true, return errors instead of calling t.Fatal
}
